title: Cloning
examples: What is the difference between cloning and natural reproduction?
Can humans be cloned with current technology?
How does a plant cutting work to make a new plant?

explain.say: Today we are learning about cloning, which means making an exact copy.

items: It is like making a photocopy.
We are looking at how this works in life.

explain.say: Dolly the sheep was a famous example of cloning in animals.

items: It was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell

draw.text: Dolly the sheep: First mammal clone

explain.say: Cloning means creating an identical copy of an organism.
Plants can also be cloned using a simple method called cuttings.

items: Place it in soil or water
A new plant grows from that piece

explain.say: In real life, farmers use cuttings to grow many plants quickly.
A common mistake is thinking cloning only works on animals.

items: It is not limited to animals.
Plants show this easily with cuttings.

draw.text: Mistake: Only animals can be cloned

faq.q: What is the main difference between cloning and natural birth?
faq.a: Natural birth involves combining DNA from two parents. Cloning creates a genetic copy from only one organism's cells.
asks: How is a clone different from a baby?

faq.q: Does a clone have the same personality as the original?
faq.a: While the DNA is identical, the environment and experiences shape the individual, so personality can differ.
asks: Will a clone act exactly like the source?
Is personality determined only by genes?

faq.q: How is the nucleus used in the cloning process?
faq.a: The nucleus contains the cell's DNA. In cloning, the nucleus from a body cell is transferred to another egg cell.
asks: What is the job of the nucleus?
Why is the nucleus important for cloning?

faq.a: Success depends on the plant type and how the cutting is cared for. Some plants root much easier than others.
asks: Does every stem piece grow into a plant?
What makes a plant cutting successful?

faq.q: Is Dolly the sheep still a relevant example?
faq.a: Dolly remains a key historical example showing the process of transferring a nucleus to create a mammal clone.
asks: Can we still study Dolly's process?
What did Dolly teach scientists about DNA?

facts: Dolly the sheep was cloned using techniques involving cell nuclei.
Cloning creates a genetic duplicate, not an exact replica of experience.
Plant cuttings use asexual reproduction to create clones.
The nucleus carries the organism's complete set of DNA.

quiz.say: If you use a piece of rosemary stem to grow a new bush, what method are you using?
quiz.why: Plant cuttings use the plant's own cells to create a new, identical plant.

wrong.0: This involves mixing DNA from two different parents.
wrong.1: Mitosis is cell division, not the entire process of growing a new plant.
wrong.2: Fertilization requires combining egg and sperm cells.

quiz.say: What does 'identical copy' mean in the context of cloning?
quiz.why: It means the DNA sequence is the same as the original organism's DNA.

wrong.0: Age is determined by time, not just DNA.
wrong.1: Memories are formed through life experiences, not just genes.
wrong.3: A clone shares DNA but grows up in a different environment.

quiz.say: Which part of the cell is transferred to start the cloning process?
quiz.why: The nucleus contains the full set of instructions, or DNA, needed to build the new organism.

wrong.0: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance, not the main genetic container.
wrong.2: Mitochondria provide energy but do not hold the core genetic blueprint.
wrong.3: The membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
